editorial.headline: The Civil Works Behind Hydropower’s Water System
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the constructed water-control infrastructure of a hydropower plant, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
A hydropower facility depends on a set of works that guide and control water before and after it passes through the plant. This activity covers construction of the reservoir, intake, control gate, penstock and outflow. Read as a whole, it concerns the built water-management infrastructure of a hydropower project: the reservoir and the structures that receive water, control its movement, carry it onward through the penstock and take it out again. Rather than describing hydropower in general, the scope identifies those precise construction elements. Its place is therefore within the project’s physical waterworks.

Registration is open at every stated enterprise scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The national PMA position is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national record allows full foreign ownership for this activity. Its cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The record presents scale access and foreign ownership together: a business at any of the four named sizes can undertake this activity when its work is the construction scope described here.

Bali’s position is equally clear, though it turns on the province’s risk-based moratorium. That rule permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the island. This activity is not marked as blocked. The Bali assessment records it as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and explains that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi — medium-high or high — and is therefore not blocked by the moratorium.

For a foreign-owned business undertaking these hydropower waterworks, the national and Bali readings align. Nationally, the activity is open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, the recorded risk position means the cited island-wide moratorium does not block it. There is no Bali-specific ownership cap or partnership condition stated in the record; the local conclusion rests on the activity’s recorded risk status and the moratorium’s stated reach.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership, this activity is not blocked by Bali’s cited moratorium.
